QM_020 states that it does not derive quantum mechanics. QM_122 recovers matrices over the Gaussian integers and leaves ordinary matrix algebras over the complex numbers unrecovered. Python, Rust, and Lean 4 must name each import and keep it imported. A finite matrix calculation is not a discharge of the import list.

This is the second law under which the inner product is selected up to scale; it is supplied, not derived from primitive difference, and sectors with distinguished labels would break it (then the diagonal is constant only on orbits).
queue.bottleneck: No finite-theory primitive forces readout invariance under sector relabelling; H006 supplies the permutation envelope only. Deriving the law, or recording which sector labels are distinguished, is item 1 of the run next steps.

queue.statement: After the finite carrier, the required dynamics are finite: an instrument or measurement update, a path sum on a finite graph, a unitary or Hamiltonian shadow on a finite matrix, and a channel that is either exact or explicitly imported. The derivation note leaves the step from stochastic kernels to completely positive maps as a gap. Python, Rust, and Lean 4 must each state the finite map and the hypothesis it uses. A numerical CPTP check at a fixed tolerance is a diagnostic. It does not authorize the exact channel.

queue.statement: Write P for the presented inscriptions and O for the internal observations. Supplying <a> after <> changes P from {<>} to {<a>} and leaves O_1 = O_0 = ∅, so no new internal distinction is available. With q : P → N sending an inscription to the distinctions the regime has, x ≠ y in P can hold while q(x) = q(y) in N, so a new presentation does not imply a new internal class, and in the other direction q(x) = q(y) does not imply x = y. Under the opaque convention <a> is a new presentation state in the same internal class as <>; the statement holds under that convention only.

queue.statement: Imported inference, audited against Marletto-Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 2-3) and Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-2): if two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 start in a separable state, interact only locally through a mediating system M (Q1 <-> M and M <-> Q2, with no direct Q1-Q2 interaction, Principle I locality), and end in an entangled state of Q1 + Q2, then M cannot be a classical medium (in Marletto-Vedral, M must have at least two disjoint incompatible observables whose union is not an information variable; in Bose et al., any mediator modeled by local operations and classical communication cannot create entanglement). The repository has no gravity model; TFQ-0084 is a finite shadow only.
queue.bottleneck: The inference (arXiv:1707.06036 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1707.06050 pp. 1-2) is an assumption of this branch. It does not use or support any repository Lean result.

information-theoretic definition of a classical mediator (assumption)
